Author and Finisher
AW-thur and FIN-ish-ur
phrase (biblical title of Christ)
From Hebrews 12:2, “Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith”; the Greek archēgos (author, leader, captain) and teleiōtēs (finisher, perfecter) joined as a title of Christ.

📖 Biblical Definition

Christ is the author and finisher of our faith—the one who begins the work of grace in the soul and infallibly carries it through to glory. The word rendered “author” bears the sense of captain, leader, and originator; the word “finisher” means perfecter, the one who brings to its appointed end. Together they declare that faith is no self-generated work but a gift begun by Christ and completed by Christ. He is the first cause and the last; He lays the foundation and sets the topstone with shoutings of grace. This is the marrow of the believer's assurance and the ground of the saints' perseverance: the same hand that opened blind eyes will not let go of the soul it has seized. As the Apostle reasons elsewhere, “he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ.” The exhortation of Hebrews is therefore to run the race with patience, “looking unto Jesus”—not unto our own faltering strength but unto Him who for the joy set before Him endured the cross and is now seated at the right hand of God. Because the race He runs in us He also finishes, the weakest believer may be bold; the One who authored faith will most surely finish it, and not one of His own shall perish.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A title of Christ as the originator and perfecter of saving faith, who begins and completes the work of grace in His people.

AUTHOR AND FINISHER, phrase (biblical title of Christ). From Hebrews 12:2; Greek archēgos (captain, originator) and teleiōtēs (perfecter).

He that first works faith in the heart and afterward carries it on to its consummation in glory.

The captain or leader who runs before His people in the way of faith and brings them safely home.

As recorded in Scripture: “Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God” (Hebrews 12:2).

By extension, the sure foundation of the believer's assurance and the ground of the saints' perseverance.

📖 Key Scripture

Heb 12:2 — "Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God."

Phi 1:6 — "Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ:"

Heb 2:10 — "For it became him, for whom are all things, and by whom are all things, in bringing many sons unto glory, to make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings."

Joh 6:39 — "And this is the Father's will which hath sent me, that of all which he hath given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up again at the last day."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition, though the truth is obscured wherever faith is reduced to a human work and salvation made to hang on man's persistence.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The title is too plainly Christ-exalting to be openly contested; the error that besets it is the older Pelagian and Arminian tendency to make man the author of his own faith and the keeper of his own soul. Where faith is treated as a self-sprung act and perseverance as a thing the believer must secure by his own grip, the comfort of the text is dissolved.

The principle to recover is monergism in beginning and end. Christ is the captain who runs first and the perfecter who finishes; He does not merely offer faith and leave its completion to us. The 1689 Confession teaches that those whom God has accepted in His Beloved can never finally fall away but shall be kept by His power through faith unto salvation. The weakest saint may therefore look away from himself and unto Jesus, certain that the One who began the work will finish it.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The title gathers the Greek images of captain and perfecter into one confession of Christ's sovereign work in faith.

expand to see more

Archēgos denotes a captain, founder, or originator who leads the way for others to follow.

Teleiōtēs denotes a finisher or perfecter who brings a thing to its appointed completion.

Hebrews 12:2 joins the two as the ground for running the Christian race with patience.

Philippians 1:6 echoes the same assurance: God will perform the work He has begun.

Hebrews 2:10 names Christ the captain of salvation, made perfect through sufferings.

Usage

"The phrase anchors the doctrine of perseverance: Christ both begins and completes saving faith."

"Believers fix their eyes on Jesus as author and finisher rather than on their own wavering strength."

"Pastors press the title to comfort fearful saints who doubt they can hold out to the end."
